$comment: CF-SCHEDULED-JOBS-CANARY exemption list (2026-09-07). Cron workflows whose
scheduled runs are red BY DESIGN and must not alarm.
THIS FILE IS THE LIST. The canary reads it; nothing is hand-typed into the
script. Adding a name here silences a real red, so each entry carries the
reason and the condition that ends the exemption — an exemption with no
exit condition is just a permanently disabled alarm.
IT IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY TODAY. #1954 triaged seven red jobs and named two
'chronic by design': Sold Comps Cleanliness Canary and Catalog Token
Coverage Canary. Neither is exempt HERE, because this canary asks a
different question than those two do. They are red about DATA (a coverage
gap wanting a backfill); a canary that alarms when a workflow's last two
scheduled runs both failed is asking whether the JOB RAN. A data-red canary
that runs and reports is working, and both of those exit non-zero on
purpose — so they belong here only if their reds are permanent, which is a
judgement for their owners, not this file's default.
The two names in the task brief were checked and BOTH are stale:
- Tier 1 Production Harness is a PULL_REQUEST check in regression.yml,
not a cron. It is never enumerated, so it cannot be exempted. Its
memory note records the 401 as RESOLVED 2026-06-30 (PR #218/#219/#221).
- Era-Baselines Refresh IS a cron and IS chronically red, but NOT on a
timeout. Verified on run 34020643605 (2026-09-06T08:00Z): it dies in
33s with 'Cannot find dist output — run `npm run build` first', the
same missing-build-step class #1954 fixed elsewhere. The timeout memory
describes pre-2026-07-16 behaviour and is marked RESOLVED. Exempting it
would hide a live, fixable defect behind a stale reason, so it is left
to alarm.
